# PetPawCalc

> Free calculators and guides for dog and cat owners in the US. PetPawCalc provides instant, research-backed answers about pet age, nutrition, weight, pregnancy, costs, and insurance — built for pet parents, not veterinarians.

PetPawCalc is a free tool-first resource. Every calculator is designed to give practical, actionable output — not just information. All content is written for US pet owners and calibrated to current veterinary guidelines. No signup required for any tool.

## Tools

- [Dog Age Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-age-calculator.html): Converts dog years to human years by size using PetMD's veterinarian-written rule — about 15 at age 1, 24 at age 2, then about 4 (small), 4–5 (medium), 5–6 (large) or 7–8 (giant) human years per year.

- [Cat Age Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-age-calculator.html): Converts cat years to human years based on feline aging research. Distinguishes between the rapid development phase (years 1–2) and the more gradual aging of adult cats.

- [Pet Food Calorie Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-food-calorie-calculator.html): Calculates daily calorie needs for dogs and cats based on weight, age, neuter status, and activity level using the Resting Energy Requirement (RER) formula.

- [Dog Weight Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-weight-calculator.html): Estimates a puppy's adult weight with PetMD's vet rules (toy/small: 6 weeks ×4 or 8 weeks ×3; medium/large: 4 months ×2), expected weekly gain from the Merck manual's 2–4 g/day per kg of adult weight, and an overweight dog's ideal weight from its body condition score (AAHA: ~10% per point above 5).

- [Annual Pet Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/annual-pet-cost-calculator.html): Builds a yearly dog or cat budget line by line from sourced US prices — Synchrony 2025–26 vet averages and PetMD test ranges, Chewy parasite-prevention prices, NAPHIA 2025 premiums, ASPCA supplies — plus the user's own food, grooming and boarding costs; each line shows its source.

- [Pet Insurance Cost Estimator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-insurance-cost-estimator.html): US average premiums by species and plan type from NAPHIA 2025 data ($836 dog / $435 cat accident-and-illness), and a comparison of the user's quote with the average and its break-even bill given deductible and reimbursement rate.

- [Dog Pregnancy Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-pregnancy-calculator.html): Counts 63 days from a mating date (normal window ±7 days) or a progesterone-timed ovulation date (±1–2 days), per Cornell. Week-by-week guide with confirmation timings (Merck, VCA), VCA feeding guidance and when to call the vet during whelping.

- [Dog Heat Cycle Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-heat-cycle-calculator.html): Dates the next heat from the last heat and the dog's usual interval (twice a year for most dogs, three times for some small breeds, once for some giant breeds, or her own interval), then the likely estrus window and end of discharge from Cornell stage averages.

- [Dog Vet Visit Scheduler](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-vet-visit-scheduler.html): Next checkup date from age, size and last visit using PetMD's schedule (every 3–4 weeks for puppies until 16–20 weeks, yearly for adults, every six months for seniors — from about 9 for small, 7 for medium and 6 for large and giant dogs), with what to raise at each visit.

- [Cat Vet Visit Scheduler](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-vet-visit-scheduler.html): Next checkup date from age, lifestyle and last visit using PetMD's schedule (every 3–4 weeks for kittens until 16–20 weeks, yearly for adults, every six months from about 10), with AAHA/AAFP vaccine and senior-screening notes for indoor and outdoor cats.

- [Cat Pregnancy Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-pregnancy-calculator.html): Counts 63–65 days from mating with VCA's normal 60–67-day range and a 71-day vet threshold. Week-by-week guide with PetMD/Merck confirmation timings, feeding and labor warning signs.

- [Cat Weight Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-weight-calculator.html): Compares a cat's weight with typical adult weights for 12 breeds by sex (APOP breed reference; PetMD for domestic shorthairs) and estimates an overweight cat's ideal weight and safe weekly loss from its body condition score (AAHA 2014).

- [Dog Quality of Life Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-quality-of-life-calculator.html): Interactive version of Alice Villalobos's HHHHHMM Quality of Life Scale (Hurt, Hunger, Hydration, Hygiene, Happiness, Mobility, More good days than bad), each scored 0–10; a total above 35 of 70 is her threshold for acceptable palliative care. Flags any single area scoring 3 or less.

- [Cat Quality of Life Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-quality-of-life-calculator.html): The HHHHHMM scale (0–10 per area, above 35 of 70 acceptable) with cat-specific cues for grooming, hiding, jumping and litter box use, and the Feline Grimace Scale's facial signs of pain. Flags any single area scoring 3 or less.

- [Cat Heat Cycle Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-heat-cycle-calculator.html): Estimates when a cat's heat ends and the next begins if she isn't mated, from VCA averages (heat about 7 days, range 1–21; whole cycle 1–6 weeks, average about 3). Notes seasonal versus year-round cycling for indoor cats.

- [Pet Weight Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-weight-calculator.html): Dog or cat body-condition weight check: the user picks a 1–9 body condition score (WSAVA/Purina descriptions) and gets an estimated ideal weight using AAHA's roughly 10% per point above 5, plus AAHA's weekly weight-loss pace (1–2% for dogs, 0.5–2% for cats). Links to the separate dog and cat weight calculators.

- [Dog Vaccination Schedule Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-vaccination-schedule-calculator.html): Enter a dog's age and lifestyle (boarding/daycare, dog parks, outdoor/rural exposure) to get a personalized vaccine status list — core vaccines (DHPP, rabies) and lifestyle-driven non-core vaccines (Bordetella, leptospirosis, canine influenza) — flagged as due, upcoming, recommended, or up to date, with typical cost ranges per vaccine. Also includes a CAPC-based deworming schedule calculator (same age input) covering the every-2-week puppy phase, monthly phase, and quarterly adult maintenance — dates/intervals only, no dosage information.

- [Cat Vaccination Schedule Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-vaccination-schedule-calculator.html): Enter a cat's age and lifestyle (indoor-only, indoor with other cats, outdoor access) to get a personalized vaccine status list — core vaccines (FVRCP, rabies) and lifestyle-driven FeLV recommendation — flagged as due, upcoming, recommended, or up to date, with typical cost ranges per vaccine. Also includes a CAPC-based deworming schedule calculator (same age input) covering the every-2-week kitten phase (starting ~3 weeks, a week later than puppies), monthly phase, and quarterly adult maintenance — dates/intervals only, no dosage information.

- [Spay/Neuter Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/spay-neuter-cost-calculator.html): National average spay/neuter prices (Synchrony 2025–26: dog $455/$487, cat $353/$262) or a low-cost clinic quote, plus pre-surgical bloodwork and microchip, what to ask a clinic, and how to find low-cost programs (SpayUSA).

- [Dental Cleaning Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dental-cleaning-cost-calculator.html): Dental bill estimate from Synchrony 2025–26 averages (cleaning $379 dog / $395 cat, chemistry panel, dental X-rays, $99 per extraction for cats, editable), why anesthesia is needed (AVDC, Merck), home care and the VOHC seal standard.

- [Pet Grooming Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-grooming-cost-calculator.html): Yearly grooming budget from a groomer's quote or a national chain's base prices (bath $30, nails/ears/teeth/glands $12 each, CareCredit Nov 2025) and visit frequency, plus AKC brushing and shaving advice.

- [Flea & Tick Prevention Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/flea-tick-prevention-cost-calculator.html): Yearly cost of Seresto, Frontline Plus, NexGard and Simparica Trio for a dog's weight band, or Seresto, Frontline Plus and Revolution Plus for cats, at Chewy prices checked November 2026.

- [Puppy Potty Training Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/puppy-potty-training-calculator.html): Maximum hold time from the AKC's month-plus-one rule, a daytime break interval (every 2–3 hours while house training, per veterinary behaviorist Kelly Ballantyne) and a daily trigger checklist (waking, meals, play, confinement, bedtime). Covers Ballantyne's steps, crates and pads, and medical causes first.

- [Kitten Litter Training Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/kitten-litter-training-timeline.html): Box, litter and setup by kitten age from Kitten Lady, PetMD and the Feline Veterinary Medical Association: a box from about 3–4 weeks, non-clumping litter until about 8–10 weeks or 2–3 months, about 1.5× body length, one box per cat plus one.

- [Raw Feeding Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/raw-feeding-calculator.html): Enter a dog or cat's weight, life stage, and raw feeding model (80/10/10 Prey Model Raw or 70/10/10+10% BARF for dogs) to get daily portions split into muscle meat, bone, and organ, plus an estimated monthly and annual cost based on meat price per pound.

- [Pet Boarding Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-boarding-cost-calculator.html): Trip-away cost using Rover's September 2025 national averages (sitter's-home boarding $49.01/night, house sitting $55.45, drop-ins $21.80) or a kennel quote, with extra pets, extras and holiday surcharges.

- [Titer Test vs. Revaccination Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/titer-test-vs-revaccination-calculator.html): Select species, years to compare, titer testing frequency, and number of pets to compare the total cost of standard core-vaccine revaccination against titer testing, showing both the best-case (all titers stay positive) and a scenario where one booster is still eventually needed.

- [Spay/Neuter Recovery Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/spay-neuter-recovery-timeline.html): Dated recovery calendar from the ASPCA Spay/Neuter Alliance's aftercare instructions: half meal on day 0, appetite within 24 hours, 7–10 days of rest, no baths for 10 days, twice-daily incision checks with what's normal for each sex and species, the 10-day recheck if skin stitches were used, and the 30-day fertility window after neutering.

- [Pet Insurance Waiting Period Tracker](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-insurance-waiting-period-tracker.html): Enter a policy's effective date and its accident/illness/orthopedic waiting periods to see the exact calendar dates each coverage type begins. Covers the pre-existing-condition trap (symptoms during the waiting period can be excluded permanently) and explains that switching insurers resets all waiting periods.

- [Neuter Timing by Breed & Size](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/neuter-timing-by-breed-size.html): Select a dog breed (21 entries: 5 mixed-breed weight categories plus 16 individually studied breeds) and sex to see a summary of what UC Davis (Hart et al., 2020/2024) research reported on joint disorder and cancer risk by neutering age — framed strictly as "what the study found," not a recommendation, with a fixed vet-consult notice on every result. Includes a weight-category risk table and a traditional-6-month-vs-research-based comparison table.

- [Cat Introduction Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-introduction-timeline.html): Enter an introduction start date, new cat type (kitten/adult), and resident cat details to get a 6-stage timeline (separate room, scent exchange, feeding near the door, site swapping, visual contact, supervised face-to-face) with date ranges plus "move forward when" / "go back if" signs for each stage. Explicitly frames dates as typical ranges, not a fixed schedule. Includes a kitten-vs-adult-introduction comparison table and a smooth-signs-vs-warning-signs table.

- [Pet Travel Timeline Planner](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-travel-timeline-planner.html): Enter a planned departure date, destination "tier" (1: no rabies antibody test / 2: antibody test with moderate wait / 3: antibody test with longest wait, rabies-free region), and whether microchip/rabies vaccine are already done, to get a reverse-calculated prep timeline (microchip → rabies vaccine → antibody blood draw → lab wait → post-result wait → health certificate/USDA endorsement). Deliberately avoids naming specific countries since requirements change; flags any calculated milestone date that has already passed. Fixed "confirm with USDA APHIS and your destination" warning shown at both page top and in the result. Covers the microchip-before-rabies-vaccine order requirement, the antibody test's multi-month impact, and the health certificate's short (~10 day) validity window. Also includes a "Don't Forget the Crate Itself" section covering the IATA CR1 crate-sizing formula (length = nose-to-tail + half elbow height, width = shoulder width × 2, height = standing height + bedding allowance) as informational content, not a separate interactive calculator, since standalone crate-size calculators are a saturated space. Bidirectionally linked with the Titer Test vs. Revaccination Calculator.

- [Dog Introduction Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-introduction-timeline.html): Enter an introduction start date, new dog type (puppy/adult), and resident dog details to get a 6-stage timeline (neutral territory first meeting, parallel walk, angled approach & brief sniff, walk home together with resident dog entering first, indoor supervised interaction with separate feeding/sleeping, gradual unsupervised time) with date ranges plus "move forward when" / "go back if" signs for each stage. Covers resource-guarding recovery (2-4 week structural separation) and post-fight restart protocol (24+ hour separation, resume from parallel walk at greater distance). Includes a puppy-vs-adult comparison table and a smooth-signs-vs-warning-signs table. Bidirectionally linked with Cat Introduction Timeline.

- [New Baby Pet Prep Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/new-baby-pet-prep-timeline.html): Enter a due date, pet species (dog/cat), and current behavior-concern status to get a reverse-calculated prep timeline (behavior foundation at ~4 months out, sound desensitization at ~3 months, gear practice/resource access review at ~2 months, carrying rehearsal/handling familiarization at ~1 month, scent exposure at the due date, first meeting a few days after homecoming). Species-specific content — dog track covers stroller/gear practice, cat track covers resource-access and vertical-space protection instead. Fixed supervision warning shown in the result. Includes a dog-vs-cat prep comparison table.

- [Puppy Teething Timeline](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/puppy-teething-timeline.html): Shows a puppy's teething stage by age from AKC and VCA timelines (28 baby teeth by 5–6 weeks, shedding from 12–16 weeks, 42 adult teeth by about 6–7 months), VCA guidance on retained baby teeth and AAHA chew-toy hardness checks.

- [Pet Insurance Claim Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-insurance-claim-calculator.html): Enter a claim amount, deductible, deductible type (annual/per-incident), reimbursement rate, and remaining annual limit to see expected reimbursement and out-of-pocket cost. The differentiator is a 5-year side-by-side comparison for a recurring/chronic condition, showing that a per-incident (lifetime per-condition) deductible is typically cheaper than an annual deductible when the same condition recurs every year — since the per-incident deductible is paid only once for that condition, while an annual deductible resets every policy year. Also explains when annual is the better choice instead (multiple unrelated conditions over time). No insurer recommendations or rankings; industry-general ranges only. Completes a 3-way bidirectional link with the Pet Insurance Cost Estimator and Pet Insurance Waiting Period Tracker.

- [Dog Car Anxiety Desensitization Planner](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-car-anxiety-desensitization-planner.html): Leads with a discriminator table distinguishing anxiety-driven car trouble (symptoms before the car moves) from true motion sickness (symptoms once moving, vestibular/inner-ear based, ~15% of adult dogs, more common in puppies whose inner ear isn't fully developed). Enter a start date, dog age group, symptom type, and severity to get a 6-stage desensitization timeline (parked car → engine on → 30-second drive → around the block → short fun drive → gradual extension) with date ranges scaled by severity, plus "move forward when"/"go back if" signs per stage. Medication names (Cerenia/maropitant, trazodone) mentioned only as vet-discussion options, never with dosing. Bidirectionally linked with the Cat Carrier Training Planner.

- [Cat Carrier Training Planner](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-carrier-training-planner.html): Enter a vet appointment date, current carrier reaction (none/wary/panics), and carrier type to get a reverse-calculated countdown plan (make the carrier furniture → feed near/inside it → reward voluntary entry → close the door briefly → carry a few steps → into the car engine-off → short practice drive), with the full window scaled by how severe the cat's reaction is. Covers why top-loading/removable-top carriers reduce stress, Feliway timing (spray 15-30 minutes ahead so the alcohol base evaporates), Fear Free certified clinics, and a "short on time" fallback section for appointments only a day or two out. Bidirectionally linked with the Dog Car Anxiety Desensitization Planner.

- [Dog Heat Safety Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-heat-safety-calculator.html): Calculates the National Weather Service heat index from temperature and humidity, estimates parked-car temperatures from the AVMA table, and lists the heatstroke risk factors that apply to a dog from UK veterinary research (Hall 2020; Beard 2024) and Cornell. Includes the RVC's 'cool first, transport second' first aid. It deliberately gives no invented safe temperature or walk time.

- [Dog Arthritis Screening Tool](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-mobility-arthritis-screening.html): A free at-home screening for early signs of arthritis in dogs, based on a validated 6-question checklist from a 500-dog veterinary study (Wright et al., 2022, Journal of Small Animal Practice). Answer yes/no to 6 items (limping/stiffness after exercise, signs of pain, reluctance to climb stairs or jump, difficulty rising from rest, change in behavior, tiring easily on walks) to get a screening result (not a diagnosis) with roughly 88% sensitivity and 71% specificity for osteoarthritis at the "any yes" threshold reported in the source study. Explicitly distinguished from the Dog Quality of Life Calculator: this tool is for early detection in dogs who seem subtly different, while the QoL calculator is for ongoing tracking in senior or already-diagnosed dogs. Links weight management (a tier-1 AAHA-recommended intervention) to the Dog Weight Calculator and Pet Food Calorie Calculator. No drug names, dosing, or supplement brand recommendations.
- [Cat Arthritis Screening Tool](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-mobility-arthritis-screening.html): A free at-home screening for signs of arthritis (degenerative joint disease) in cats, implementing the validated Feline Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Checklist (Enomoto, Lascelles & Gruen, 2020, Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery), developed from data on 300+ cats. Six yes/no items ask whether the cat still jumps up, jumps down, climbs up stairs, climbs down stairs, runs, and chases moving objects NORMALLY — note the inverted polarity versus the dog tool: here a "no" is the flagged answer, and the source study proposes that any single "no" should prompt further evaluation. Explains why cats are screened differently from dogs (feline joint disease is frequently bilateral, so limping is usually absent; only a small minority of cats with radiographic joint changes show lameness). Also covers signs not on the checklist (grooming decline, litter box accidents, abandoned high resting spots), role separation from the Cat Quality of Life Calculator (this tool = detection in undiagnosed cats; QoL = tracking already-diagnosed cats), weight as a first-line factor, and acute red flags that warrant same-day care. No drug names, dosing, or supplement brands; explicitly warns that human and canine painkillers are toxic to cats.
- [Elimination Diet Trial Planner](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/elimination-diet-trial-planner.html): Dated planner for an 8-week elimination diet trial in dogs and cats with a one-week transition and challenge phase, based on Olivry, Mueller and Prélaud's 2015 critically appraised topic (over 95% of dogs and about 90% of cats in remission by 8 weeks). Includes a contamination audit (flavored preventives and medications, treats, other pets' food) and notes that serum and saliva food-allergy tests aren't reliable (Mueller and Olivry, 2017).
- [Pet Itch Score Tracker](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-itch-score-tracker.html): Free itch severity scoring tool for dogs and cats implementing the owner-assessed pruritus visual analog scale (Hill, Lau & Rybníček, Vet Dermatol 2007;18:301-308; further validated by Rybníček et al., Vet Dermatol 2009;20:115-122 in 713 owners). Deliberately hides the numeric value while the owner positions the slider, because the 2009 validation found owners were heavily influenced by visible numerical markings, which degraded the scale's continuous data; behavioural descriptors are shown instead and the 0–10 score is revealed only after committing. Notes that a separate 0–10 verbal numeric scale was validated in 2022 (251 dogs) but is not interchangeable with the pVAS, and that a separate feline pruritus VAS exists. Measures severity only, never cause. Flags the ~50% reduction benchmark used to judge elimination diet trial response, prompts for secondary skin infection at high scores, prompts cat owners to check belly/inner thigh fur loss from covert over-grooming, and always reminds the user to verify flea control. Stores nothing between sessions.
- [Dog Cold Weather Safety Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-cold-weather-safety-calculator.html): Calculates the National Weather Service wind chill from air temperature and wind speed, and lists the cold-weather risk factors that apply to a dog from Cornell, the AVMA and Anchorage Animal Care and Control's screening tool (rain or sleet weighted double). Covers signs of cold, frostbite, coats, paws, salt and antifreeze. No invented safe-time estimate.
- [Orphaned Kitten & Puppy Bottle Feeding Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/orphaned-kitten-puppy-bottle-feeding-calculator.html): Formula per feed, feeds per day and nest temperature from weight and age. Kittens: about 27 ml per 100 g a day (Maddie's-based chart), a 4 ml/100 g stomach-capacity check with the ASPCA's double-capacity limit, Pasadena Humane/Kitten Lady feeding intervals and National Kitten Coalition nest temperatures. Puppies: VCA calorie needs (15/20/25 kcal per 100 g by age) divided by the formula label's kcal per ml. A warm-first gate stops the plan for a cold animal.
- [Kitten Age Estimator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/kitten-age-estimator.html): Free tool that estimates a kitten's age range from developmental signs — umbilical cord, eyes (closed, opening, open and blue, colour changing), ears, teeth (none, incisors, canines, full baby set, adult teeth erupting, full adult set), movement and eating — plus optional weight, and gives an approximate birth date. Finds the age window consistent with all answers; when answers conflict it sets aside the least reliable sign first (weight, then eating, then movement), trusting teeth, eyes and ears most, and flags weight that lags development as a possible sign of underfeeding, parasites or illness. Shows age-appropriate care (feeding interval, toileting stimulation, weaning, deworming from about 3 weeks, FVRCP from 6–8 weeks, spay/neuter at 4–6 months) and a reference table of milestones (eyes open 8–14 days, ears up ~3 weeks, baby incisors 2.5–3.5 weeks, canines 3–4, premolars 5–8, adult teeth 3–6 months).
- [Cat Urinary Emergency Checker](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/cat-urinary-emergency-checker.html): Free urgency triage tool for cats showing urinary signs. Asks four questions — sex, how much urine is produced when straining, accompanying signs, and duration — and returns one of three urgency bands. DESIGNED TO ESCALATE ONLY: there is no branch that tells the user to stay home; the mildest available outcome is "book an appointment", and the page opens with a banner telling anyone whose cat is straining and producing nothing to stop reading and call an emergency vet. Built around the specific error that kills cats: the AVMA notes that straining in the litter box, though it looks like constipation, is more often a sign the urethra is blocked — a constipated cat still passes urine normally, a blocked cat passes little or none. Covers why male cats block (longer, narrower urethra; AVMA notes obstruction is most often found in males aged 1–10), that complete obstruction becomes life-threatening within roughly 24–48 hours, that it never resolves on its own, and what FLUTD covers (feline idiopathic cystitis, obstruction, stones/crystals, bacterial infection). Tells users not to press the abdomen and to say the phrase "possible urinary blockage" when phoning. Explicitly states it cannot rule an emergency out.
- [Lost Pet Search Plan](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/lost-pet-search-plan.html): Free search-plan generator for a missing cat or dog. Takes species, indoor-only vs outdoor-access (cats), temperament and time missing, and returns a search radius plus a numbered priority order. Built around the finding that owners' instinctive first move — driving around calling, then flyers, then the shelter — is close to backwards for cats. Cites Huang, Rand, Albrecht et al., Animals 2018;8(1):5 (n=1,210 missing cats): 75% found within 500 m of the escape point, ~18% hiding directly outside an entrance to their own home, indoor-only cats a median of 50 m (~2.5 house radius), ~34% recovered alive by the owner within 7 days and ~56% by two months. Notes honestly that the same study's physical-searching benefit reached only p=0.073, short of conventional significance, because that figure circulates online as settled fact. Explains Kat Albrecht's "Silence Factor" (a sick or frightened cat hides without calling out, so a calling search fails). For dogs the emphasis is DO NOT CHASE — any forward movement counts, including following by car; a panicked dog behaves like prey and reads humans as predators; the alternative is to sit or lie down, turn side-on, avoid eye contact, toss treats sideways and let the dog touch you first. Also covers the shelter mismatch: the shelter is the owner's first stop and often the finder's last.
- [Ear Infection Recurrence Checker](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/ear-infection-recurrence-checker.html): For dogs and cats with recurring ear infections, structured on the veterinary PSPP framework (primary, secondary, predisposing, perpetuating). Uses a 2025 Today's Veterinary Practice review (atopic dermatitis in 43–75% of canine otitis externa; cytology as the most valuable test; hidden otitis media in about 1 in 5 chronic cases) and food-allergy data cited in dvm360, and lists questions to ask the vet.
- [Dog & Cat Diarrhea Triage and Feeding Plan](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/pet-diarrhea-triage-and-feeding-plan.html): Free triage tool for dogs and cats with diarrhoea, taking species, age/health group, stool appearance, vomiting, energy, duration and vaccination status, and returning one of three urgency bands plus explicit feeding guidance. CENTRAL POINT: the widely repeated advice to withhold food for 24 hours has largely been overturned — VCA Animal Hospitals states that fasting for GI upset was once standard on the belief the gut needed rest, but it is now understood the gut needs nutrients while recovering and withholding food can cause more damage and delay recovery; PetMD adds that a dog with diarrhoea and no vomiting has no need to be fasted. The page is explicit that this is not fully settled — some clinics still advise a short fast of up to 12 hours for a healthy adult with mild uncomplicated diarrhoea — and says to follow your own vet for your own pet. Fasting is flagged as never appropriate for cats (hepatic lipidosis risk), puppies and kittens, toy and small breeds, seniors, diabetics, or pets with existing conditions. Emergency triggers: melena (black tarry stool) always; raspberry-jam diarrhoea (AHDS/HGE, most often small and toy breeds, shock within hours); puppy or unvaccinated dog; repeated vomiting; lethargy or not drinking. Warns against loperamide and bismuth products without veterinary approval, noting bismuth turns stool black and destroys the ability to spot melena, and that some herding breeds are genetically sensitive to common human drugs.
- [Dog Separation Anxiety Screener](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/dog-separation-anxiety-screener.html): Free two-stage screener. STAGE ONE checks the mimics before separation anxiety, because most dogs labelled with it have something else: confinement distress / barrier frustration (panic about the crate specifically, occurring even when a person is home — veterinary behaviour guidance says the first step is filming the dog alone OUTSIDE the crate); boredom (settles and sleeps first, then destroys random items, and chews while the owner is in the next room); isolation distress (fine with any company, versus separation anxiety proper which is attachment to one specific person); incomplete house training and territorial marking (soiling in varied circumstances rather than departure-only); and medical causes (urinary disease, GI disease, pain, cognitive dysfunction). Routes to "film it first" when the owner has never watched a departure, since without video there is no threshold and any plan is guesswork. STAGE TWO, only when the screen is consistent with SA or isolation distress, gives a starting threshold and a six-step plan. Central point: SUSPENDING ABSENCES — not leaving the dog alone longer than they can currently handle — is what decides whether training works, because under-threshold practice three times a week alongside eight-hour absences is a treadmill where each panic episode undoes progress. Also states that crating usually worsens SA (most patients do not improve; dogs break teeth escaping), that "leave them to get used to it" is flooding rather than desensitisation, that punishment is counterproductive and dogs do not act from spite, and that treatment takes months with starting durations measured in seconds — explicitly cautioning against quick-fix claims. Recommends veterinary exam first and notes medication is a legitimate veterinary decision.
- [Sleeping Respiratory Rate Counter](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/sleeping-respiratory-rate-counter.html): Tap-to-count tool with a 30-second timer for a dog's or cat's sleeping respiratory rate. Interprets the rate against VCA Hospitals' owner guide (15–30 breaths per minute normal at sleep or calm rest; consistently above 30 is increased), with study data from a cardiologist's review in Clinician's Brief (healthy dogs average about 14 asleep; a 25% rise from baseline may matter). Readings after activity, panting or purring are flagged; laboured breathing, pale or bluish gums, collapse, open-mouth breathing or sudden back-leg weakness in cats return an emergency verdict. Optional log stored only in the user's browser.
- [Separation Anxiety Training Setup Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/separation-anxiety-training-setup-checklist.html): Free interactive 21-item checklist for everything that has to be in place before departure training starts, since most plans fail on decisions made before day one. Five sections: medical rule-out and the medication conversation; the video baseline (record a normal departure, note the exact minute distress begins, film alone outside the crate to test for confinement distress, test whether any company solves it, write down the threshold); the coverage plan (map every hour of a normal week to somebody — housemate, neighbour, daycare, walker, work-from-home, dog comes along — plus backup for the days it breaks); household agreement (nobody punishes it, nobody "tests" progress with a long absence); and the four things that quietly undo it (crating unless video shows it helps, relying on tiring the dog out, anti-bark collars, and flooding). Ends with session logging, deciding in advance that a bad session means the next is shorter, and expectations set at months rather than weeks. Pairs with the Separation Anxiety Screener.
- [Dog & Cat Stool Chart: Colour and Consistency Guide](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-cat-stool-chart-color-guide): The Purina 1–7 fecal score (2 ideal), what black, red, grey and yellow stool can mean (PetMD), raspberry-jam hemorrhagic diarrhea (Merck), mucus, tapeworm segments (CDC), swallowed string, and when to call the vet.
- [How Much Exercise Does a Puppy Need? What the 5-Minute Rule Gets Wrong](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/puppy-exercise-5-minute-rule/): Article on puppy exercise and joint health. States plainly that the widely repeated "5 minutes of exercise per month of age" rule has no study behind the specific number. Reports the research that does exist: Krontveit et al., American Journal of Veterinary Research 2012;73(6):838–846, a prospective cohort of 501 puppies from 103 litters across four large breeds (Newfoundland, Labrador Retriever, Leonberger, Irish Wolfhound), which associated stair use before three months with higher radiographic hip dysplasia risk and off-lead exercise on soft, moderately uneven ground with LOWER risk — so over-restricting a puppy is not the safe default the rule implies. Frames risk by type of activity (self-directed vs forced pace, soft vs hard ground, varied vs repetitive impact) rather than minutes, and explains why the site deliberately did not build a puppy exercise calculator: it would turn a rule of thumb into false precision and give the same answer for a Chihuahua and a Great Dane. Is explicit that the evidence covers four large breeds and should not be stretched to toy breeds. Identifies weight as the larger lever, citing Sallander et al. (J Nutr 2006) on free-choice feeding and long-term Labrador feeding research on lean body condition.
- [Heartworm Test Cost — and Why a Negative Result Is Months Out of Date](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/heartworm-test-cost/): Article on heartworm testing cost (antigen test about $35–$75 at a private clinic, less at low-cost clinics; microfilaria test $20–$40; possible exam fee) built around the detection lag: per the American Heartworm Society, larvae take about 6 months to mature and heartworms must be roughly 7 months old before an infection can be diagnosed, so a negative result reflects status months ago. Applies that to puppies under 7 months (start prevention without a test; test 6 months later, 6 months after that, then yearly), missed doses (restart prevention, retest 6 months later — a test the same month cannot answer whether the missed dose mattered), and dogs on year-round prevention (annual testing confirms the program works; manufacturer guarantees such as the Zoetis ProHeart guarantee require documented negative tests). Explains antigen-test false negatives (few, male-only or immature worms; antibody-bound antigen) and the AHS recommendation to pair antigen with microfilaria testing. Covers cats separately: typically one to three worms and often none adult, antigen plus antibody screening, and no approved treatment. Pairs with the Heartworm Prevention Cost Calculator.
- [Heartworm Treatment Cost for Dogs — and Why the Cheaper-Looking Option Isn't](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/heartworm-treatment-cost/): Itemized heartworm treatment cost (PetMD ranges: confirmatory test, chest X-rays, optional echocardiogram, doxycycline, steroids, three melarsomine injections with hospital time, follow-up tests), summing to roughly $700–$2,000 for an uncomplicated case and over $3,000 for large dogs or advanced disease; surgical removal $3,000–$6,000. Explains that melarsomine is weight-dosed, so bigger dogs cost more. Lays out the AHS protocol timeline (preventive and doxycycline from diagnosis, injections around days 60, 90 and 91, tests around day 120 and nine months) and the exercise restriction. Reports the American Heartworm Society's position that 'slow kill' is a salvage procedure, not a treatment of choice: it can take a year or longer, is less effective, and lets lung damage continue. Covers insurance limits (pre-existing exclusion), manufacturer guarantees, and the absence of an approved adult-worm treatment for cats.
- [ProHeart 12 Cost: The Yearly Heartworm Shot vs Monthly Chews, by Dog Weight](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/proheart-12-cost/): ProHeart 12 injection prices by weight from published clinic price lists (up to 25 lb $78–$150; 26–50 lb $105–$160; 51–75 lb $135–$190; 76–100 lb $154–$246; over 100 lb $155–$345+) compared with Heartgard Plus online prices (about $146–$151 a year), plus the annual test ($35–$75) and exam. Compliance data: dogs averaged about 7 months of heartworm medication purchased per year and about a third had 11–12 months (Lavan et al. 2018); Zoetis-funded analysis of 6-month injectable vs monthly repurchase (Mwacalimba et al. 2021). Label restrictions (12 months+, not for sick/underweight dogs or after prior reaction, caution with vaccines), US field-study reaction rates, the ProHeart 6 2004 withdrawal and risk-management program, the Zoetis guarantee, and what it doesn't cover.
- [Felycin-CA1 Cost for Cats With HCM — and What the Evidence Behind It Actually Shows](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/felycin-ca1-cost-cat-hcm/): Weekly sirolimus (0.3 mg/kg) conditionally approved by the FDA on March 14, 2025 for ventricular hypertrophy in subclinical feline HCM. Cost by weight band at online prices (0.4 mg $4.44, 1.2 mg $150.74/12, 2.4 mg $251.26/12): about $54, $74 and $91 a month ($650–$1,090 a year), plus echocardiogram ($400–$1,200) and liver/glucose bloodwork. Pilot study of 43 cats (wall thickness −0.17 mm on label dose vs +0.94 mm placebo over 6 months; endpoint not prespecified; one cat developed diabetes; no survival data), contraindicated in diabetes, liver screening, HALT study for full approval.
- [IVDD Surgery Cost vs Crate Rest: What Each Costs, and the Recovery Odds by Severity](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/ivdd-surgery-cost-vs-crate-rest/): Specialist all-in IVDD surgery about $10,000–$15,000; MRI with CSF tap $3,000–$3,500 and neurology consult $200–$300 (University of Wisconsin, 2021); surgery-only quotes $2,000–$8,000. Recovery of walking by deep pain status: meta-analysis (Langerhuus & Miles 2017, 1,810 dogs) 93% surgery vs 62–79% conservative with deep pain, 61% vs 10% without; prospective conservative cohort (Khan, Jeffery & Freeman 2024, 72 dogs) 96% with deep pain (median 11 days), 48% without. Surgery within 24–48 hours of sensory loss, 4–6 weeks strict rest, breeds (73% chondrodystrophic; Dachshunds 25%), recurrence about 6% after surgery (Dachshunds 10%).
- [Zenrelia vs Apoquel Cost: The Once-Daily Allergy Tablet, the Vaccine Rule, and the Head-to-Head Trial](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/zenrelia-vs-apoquel-cost/): Zenrelia (ilunocitinib) prices ($2.84/tablet for 4.8 mg ×30 at Chewy; $2.18/tablet for 15 mg ×90 at PetSmart; about $65–$85 a month on one tablet a day), Vetster monthly ranges by dog size, first-month comparison with Apoquel's twice-daily start. Forster et al. 2025 (338 dogs, Elanco-funded): itch −68.2% vs −59.4% at day 28, itch remission 77% vs 53% at day 112. Boxed vaccine warning (stop ≥28 days to 3 months before, restart ≥28 days after); fatal vaccine-induced disease language removed from US label in September 2025.
- [Cat Hyperthyroidism Treatment Cost: Why the Priciest Option Is Often the Cheapest](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/cat-hyperthyroidism-treatment-cost/): Compares the four treatments for feline hyperthyroidism by cost: radioiodine (I-131) about $1,200–$2,000 one-time and curative in over 95% of cats per the 2016 AAFP guidelines; methimazole about $40–$80 a month plus rechecks every 4–6 months, roughly $640–$1,410 a year; iodine-restricted diet $80–$120 a month and only workable as the cat's sole food; thyroidectomy $1,500–$3,000. Shows the arithmetic by which lifelong medication overtakes radioiodine within about one to three years, and explains why vets still start with a methimazole trial: treating hyperthyroidism can unmask chronic kidney disease, and the trial is reversible. Prevalence up to 10% of cats over 10.
- [Cat Diabetes Treatment Cost: Insulin vs the Once-Daily Oral Drugs, and Why the First Months Matter Most](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/cat-diabetes-treatment-cost/): Itemized cost of feline diabetes: diagnosis $200–$500, insulin about $30–$150 a month, syringes, home meter and strips, rechecks with fructosamine $100–$250, diet $30–$100 a month; first year roughly $1,700–$6,400 and a stable year $1,200–$4,800; diabetic ketoacidosis hospitalization $1,500–$5,000. Explains why the first months matter: remission is reported in roughly 17–67% of insulin-treated cats, most often early, and is more likely with short duration, tight control and a low-carbohydrate diet. Compares insulin with the oral SGLT2 inhibitors Bexacat and Senvelgo (Bexacat launch list price about $53 a month, typically $100–$150 at clinics) and the FDA restriction that they are not for cats previously treated with insulin, making the choice at diagnosis one-way, plus the required ketone monitoring. Notes the 2018 AAHA guideline position that in-hospital glucose curves are not recommended for cats, favouring home testing.
- [Cat Kidney Disease Cost by Stage — and What a High SDMA Result Actually Means](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/cat-kidney-disease-cost-by-stage/): Feline chronic kidney disease costs by IRIS stage, using the IRIS cat cut-offs (creatinine <1.6, 1.6–2.8, 2.9–5.0, >5.0 mg/dL; SDMA <18, 18–25, 26–38, >38 µg/dL). Itemized costs: diagnosis $200–$500, rechecks $150–$300 every 3–6 months, renal diet $30–$125 a month, home subcutaneous fluids $30–$100 a month vs about $25+ per clinic session, medications $15–$150 a month, IV-fluid hospitalization $1,000–$3,000 per crisis. Estimated yearly totals: stage 1 $300–$1,200, stage 2 $660–$3,300, stage 3 $1,830–$5,580, stage 4 $200–$500+ a month. Evidence for the renal diet (Ross 2006 randomized trial: no uremic crises or renal deaths on kidney diet; Elliott 2000: 633 vs 264 days) and IRIS advice to transition over three weeks and not while ill. Explains high SDMA with normal creatinine (muscle loss lowers creatinine; SDMA rises after ~40% function loss; repeat in two weeks with urine specific gravity; persistent SDMA >14 with dilute urine = IRIS stage 1). Median survival by stage from Boyd 2008 (1,151 / 778 / 103 days).
- [Rabbit Spay and Neuter Cost — and Why the Cheapest Quote Isn't Always the Best Deal](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/rabbit-spay-neuter-cost/): Rabbit neuter typically $390–$550 (low-cost from about $150); spay reported from about $140 to $1,500 depending on location; House Rabbit Society Richmond clinic $200–$300. Explains the price gap with cats using CEPSAF anesthetic death risk (rabbits 1.39%, healthy 0.73%; cats 0.24%; dogs 0.17%) and lists questions to ask a vet (rabbit caseload, no pre-op fasting because rabbits can't vomit, pain relief and gut support, warming). Uterine cancer risk from Mäkitaipale et al. 2022 (116 rabbits: malignant uterine tumors in 40% of rabbits over three, ~19x the odds of younger rabbits) rather than the untraceable 'up to 80%' figure. Timing (sexual maturity 3.5–9 months; HRS minimums 2.5 months male, 5 months female), males fertile about 30 days after neuter, spaying older rabbits, recovery and GI stasis costs ($200–$600 outpatient, over $1,000 hospitalized).
- [Dog Dementia: The Signs, the Night-Time Problem, and What Treatment Costs](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-dementia-signs-treatment-cost/): Canine cognitive dysfunction: prevalence (estimated 14.2% of dogs 8+ vs 1.9% diagnosed; 28% at 11–12, 68% at 15–16 years), Dog Aging Project findings (Yarborough 2022, 15,019 dogs: odds +52% per year of age, not-active dogs ~6.5x the odds of very active dogs, eye/ear disorders ~2x). Signs grouped by disorientation, interactions, sleep-wake, house soiling, activity, anxiety and memory, versus normal aging. Conditions to rule out first (pain, vision/hearing loss, hypertension, dental/kidney/bladder disease, endocrine and brain disease). Practical steps for night-time waking. Treatments with evidence: selegiline (only FDA-approved drug for CCD; onset 4–12 weeks; drug interactions), antioxidant and MCT diets, supplements, enrichment. Costs: workup $160–$490; selegiline about $40–$50 a month for small dogs and $110–$130 for large dogs.
- [Librela Cost for Dogs — How It Compares With Daily Arthritis Pills, and What the 2025 Label Change Means](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/librela-cost-for-dogs/): Librela (bedinvetmab), a monthly anti-NGF monoclonal antibody injection for canine osteoarthritis pain approved by the FDA on May 5, 2023. Cost about $75–$300+ per injection by body weight, roughly $900–$3,600 a year, plus possible per-visit fees ($50–$100) and baseline bloodwork. Compared with daily generic carprofen (around 50 cents a tablet at some pet pharmacies) and when the higher price makes sense (dogs that can't take NSAIDs, pill refusal). Efficacy from Corral et al. 2021 (287 dogs: 43.5% vs 16.9% placebo success at day 28). Safety: FDA Dear Veterinarian letter of December 16, 2024 (ataxia, seizures, neurologic signs, polyuria/polydipsia, deaths) and the early-2025 label update adding a post-approval experience section and a client information sheet to discuss before each injection; Zoetis-reported rate about 1–10 adverse events per 10,000 doses, with the caveat of voluntary reporting.
- [Apoquel vs Cytopoint Cost: Which Is Cheaper Depends on Your Dog's Weight](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/apoquel-vs-cytopoint-cost/): Explains why the cheaper allergy treatment flips with dog size: Apoquel (oclacitinib) is priced per tablet with strengths often priced alike, so cost follows the label tablet chart (½ to 2 tablets a day; about $44–$176 a month at ~$2.94 a tablet, first month higher because of 14 days of twice-daily dosing), while Cytopoint (lokivetmab) is dosed by weight ($50–$100 per injection small dogs to $200–$300+ giant, every 4–8 weeks; about $325–$3,900 a year). Covers onset, age limits (Apoquel 12 months and 3 kg), seasonal use, and Zenrelia (ilunocitinib, approved September 2024; boxed warning on inadequate vaccine response, stop 28 days to 3 months before and 28 days after vaccination; fatal vaccine-induced disease warning later removed). Points to fleas, elimination diet trials and ear infections as the causes to address.

Evidence on surgery vs conservative care: Vasseur 1984 (86% of dogs under 15 kg normal or improved without surgery vs 19% over 15 kg), Wucherer 2013 randomized trial of overweight dogs over 20 kg (75% vs 64% success at one year). Contralateral risk: Muir 2011 (380 dogs, median 947 days to second-knee rupture) and 27.5% within the Wucherer trial year. Recovery (8–12 weeks restriction, X-ray rechecks every 4–6 weeks) and the bilateral-condition insurance exclusion.

Budget per guinea pig ($50–$150 routine, $300–$500 emergency fund, $20–$30 a month) doubled because they are kept in pairs. The three costliest problems: continuously growing teeth, bladder stones, and ovarian cysts (reported in 76–90% of adult females at post-mortem). Merck vitamin C requirement (at least 10 mg/kg/day, 30 mg/kg pregnant), unlimited hay, weekly weighing, and emergency signs.

Explains why cats have few alternatives: US injectable meloxicam is approved only as a single pre-surgical dose and carries an FDA boxed warning (repeated use linked to acute renal failure and death); robenacoxib is limited to 3 days. Reports the approval study honestly (77% of owners saw improvement vs 67% on placebo) and recommends tracking specific behaviours. Prevalence (60% of cats over 6, 90% over 12), side effects, and low-cost home changes (low-entry litter box, ramps, weight control).
- [Dog Cataract Surgery Cost — and Why Timing (and Diabetes) Changes the Bill](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-cataract-surgery-cost/): Veterinary ophthalmologist cataract surgery (phacoemulsification) costs about $2,700–$4,900: roughly $2,800–$3,800 for one eye and $3,800–$4,900 for both, the second eye adding about $500–$1,200; plus ERG ($250–$410), ocular ultrasound ($220–$800), bloodwork and rechecks. Success about 80–90% (85–90% uncomplicated), best before the cataract matures and before lens-induced uveitis; a working retina is required. Diabetes link from Beam et al. 1999 (200 diabetic dogs: ~50% cataracts by 170 days, 75% by 370 days). Aftercare (drops four or more times daily, cone, rechecks), complications, the ongoing cost of not operating (anti-inflammatory drops, glaucoma risk), and bilateral-condition insurance exclusions.

Testing per the 2023 AAHA endocrinopathy guidelines (test only with two or more supportive findings; LDDST preferred; ACTH stim can miss up to 41% of adrenal-dependent cases; UCCR to rule out) and the overdiagnosis concern from a 2025 European vet survey (about 60% screened dogs without supportive signs). Monitoring schedule (10–14 days, 30 days, then about every 90 days), pre-pill cortisol as a cheaper option, over-suppression warning signs, and survival data from Nagata et al. 2017 (untreated median 506 days; 2-year survival 52.2% treated vs 8.5% untreated).

- [Dog Diabetes Treatment Cost — and What the 2026 AAHA Guidelines Changed](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-diabetes-treatment-cost/): Itemized costs for diabetic dogs (diagnosis $225–$500, insulin $40–$80 a month small dogs and $80–$150 large, syringes, meter and strips, optional CGM sensors, rechecks $100–$250, diet); first year about $1,850–$6,200, stable year $1,300–$4,600. Explains why the aspirate comes first (lipomas and mast cell tumors feel alike; ACVS: aspirates diagnose mast cell tumors accurately in almost all cases; MCTs are 14–21% of skin tumors), the oncologists' 'See something, do something' rule (pea-sized lump present a month), what drives mast cell tumor cost (proportional margins up to 2 cm, grade, staging, radiation/chemo, tigilanol tiglate), when fatty lumps are worth removing, and cost-saving habits.

Reports the EPIC trial (Boswood et al., JVIM 2016; 360 dogs 4–15 kg with enlarged hearts and no heart failure): pimobendan delayed heart failure or cardiac death to a median 1,228 vs 766 days, about 15 months; no equivalent evidence for stage B1. - [Cat Heart Murmur: What It Does and Doesn't Mean](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/cat-heart-murmur-what-it-means/): Reports the CatScan study (780 apparently healthy cats: ~41% had murmurs, ~70% of those functional, HCM in 14.7%, murmur positive predictive value for HCM 18–43%) and Nakamura et al. 2011 (53% of 32 healthy-looking cats with murmurs had heart disease on echo). Explains why cat murmurs are unreliable both ways and that absence of a murmur does not exclude cardiomyopathy. Echocardiogram as the definitive test, NT-proBNP as screening, why X-rays help less in cats. Stage B2 (left atrial enlargement) cats are typically started on clopidogrel to reduce clot risk. Predisposed breeds, pre-anaesthetic screening, emergency signs including open-mouth breathing and sudden back-leg paralysis.
- [Pyometra in Dogs: How Common It Is, What It Costs, and Why It Changes the Spay Decision](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/pyometra-in-dogs-cost/): Swedish insurance data: about 24% of unspayed female dogs develop pyometra by age 10, over half in some large breeds (Bernese Mountain Dog 66%, Great Dane 62%, Leonberger 61%, Rottweiler 58%, Irish Wolfhound 58%); mean age about 7; most cases within three months of the start of the last heat (mean 5–6 weeks). Open vs closed pyometra (closed has no discharge and is more dangerous). Cost comparison: routine spay $200–$700 vs pyometra surgery about $500–$2,500 at general practice before diagnostics and hospitalization, often over $3,000 for emergency cases. Points out that several breeds where delayed spaying is discussed (per UC Davis neuter-timing research) are those with the highest pyometra rates. Medical treatment recurrence 20–70% within two years. Cats about 2.2% by 13.
- [Recurring Ear Infections: Vet Visit Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/recurring-ear-infection-vet-visit-checklist.html): Free interactive 20-item preparation and question checklist for appointments about repeat otitis in dogs and cats. Build the history (dated episode log, which ear each time, what was prescribed and whether it fully cleared, photos, skin signs, seasonality, full food list including treats and flavoured medications); on the day (do NOT clean the ears for 48 hours beforehand — the discharge is the diagnostic sample — and bring whatever has already been used); ask about the infection (cytology at THIS episode not just the first, eardrum integrity, whether a culture is warranted); ask about the cause (what the suspected primary cause is, whether an elimination diet trial fits, possible middle ear involvement, when dermatology referral makes sense); and afterwards (book the recheck before leaving, finish the full course, never reuse leftover drops, agree a maintenance plan since over-cleaning is itself a predisposing factor). Progress tracker and printable. Pairs with the Ear Infection Recurrence Checker.
- [Lost Pet: First 24 Hours Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/lost-pet-first-24-hours-checklist.html): Free interactive 22-item action checklist for the first day a cat or dog goes missing, ordered by yield rather than by topic: search inside again → own property with a torch → neighbours' property with permission and doing the searching yourself → the two species-specific mistakes (never chase a loose dog; never rely on calling for a cat) → microchip registry update and missing flag → shelter and vet reports with in-person visits → scent station, smelly wet food and a motion camera at the escape point → large high-visibility signs rather than small flyers → asking the public for sightings rather than for a search party → withholding one identifying detail to screen false claims → sighting log, night search, humane trap, and someone covering the phone and house. Progress tracker and printable. Pairs with the Lost Pet Search Plan.
- [Cat Urinary Health Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/cat-urinary-health-checklist.html): Free interactive 20-item prevention checklist for cats prone to lower urinary tract disease, organised around multimodal environmental modification (MEMO; Buffington et al., Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery 2006, Ohio State) and the AAFP/ISFM five pillars of a healthy feline environment (JFMS 2013). Four sections: litter boxes (one per cat plus one extra, spread rather than grouped, unscented clumping litter, scooped daily, sized ~1.5× body length with a low entry, not in a dead end), water and diet (moist food above ~60% moisture per veterinary FLUTD management guidance, 7–10 day transitions, multiple water stations away from food, bowl-vs-fountain preference testing, prescription urinary diets only when a vet prescribes them), stress (hiding places, vertical space, separated resources in multi-cat homes, daily predictable play, identifying specific stressors, never punishing out-of-box urination), and weight/monitoring (vet-guided weight loss, establishing a litter box baseline, emergency signs, follow-up urinalysis). Progress tracker and printable. Pairs with the Cat Urinary Emergency Checker.
- [Found an Orphaned Kitten? First 24 Hours Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/found-orphaned-kitten-checklist.html): Free interactive 20-item triage checklist ordered by clinical priority rather than by topic: (1) whether the kittens need rescuing at all — mother cats leave litters for hours and removing them is usually the wrong call absent immediate danger; (2) warmth, gradually over 1–3 hours, with no direct heat contact and no heat lamps, and nothing fed until fully warm; (3) assessment — skin-tent hydration test, gram-scale weighing with a written log, age estimated from eyes/ears/umbilical cord rather than weight; (4) feeding — correct milk replacer, fed belly-down never on the back, stimulation after every feed; (5) nest setup with warm and cool zones, littermates together, isolation from resident pets; (6) vet within 24 hours plus the emergency signs that mean go immediately. Progress tracker and printable. Pairs with the bottle feeding calculator.
- [Winter Pet Safety Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/winter-pet-safety-checklist.html): Free interactive 22-item cold-season checklist for dogs and cats across six sections — toxic hazards, the car check, paws and coat, outdoors, indoors, and before-first-snow. Emphasises that most winter pet injuries come from antifreeze, ice-melt salt, frozen water and slippery floors rather than from air temperature itself. Notes that "pet-safe" ice melt is a marketing term rather than a regulated one and that rinsing paws after walks is the reliable protection; that double coats should not be shaved because they insulate by trapping air; that indoor dogs on shortened winter walks usually need fewer calories rather than more; and that straw insulates community-cat shelters where blankets and hay do not. Progress tracker and printable. Pairs with the Dog Cold Weather Safety Calculator.

- [Heartworm Prevention Cost Calculator](https://petpawcalc.com/tools/heartworm-prevention-cost-calculator.html): A year of Heartgard Plus or Simparica Trio (Chewy, Nov 2026) or a ProHeart 12 injection (clinic price lists) for the dog's weight, plus the $35–$75 annual test, compared with $700–$2,000+ heartworm treatment; shows the cost of the 7-month average from purchase-record research.

## Checklists

Interactive, printable checklists at https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/. Each has checkboxes that save progress in the browser (localStorage) and a print/PDF view. Unlike the Tools section (dog/cat only), Checklists cover a wider range of companion animals.

- [New Puppy Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/new-puppy-checklist.html): Supplies, first vet visit, core vaccine series timing (6-16 weeks), socialization window (closes ~16 weeks), spay/neuter timing, and first-year budgeting.
- [New Kitten Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/new-kitten-checklist.html): Supplies, litter box setup (one per cat plus one extra), first vet visit, FeLV/FIV testing, core FVRCP vaccine series timing, toxic plant warnings (lilies), and first-year budgeting.
- [New Rabbit Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/new-rabbit-checklist.html): Housing space requirements, diet (unlimited hay + measured pellets), litter-safe products (never clumping cat litter), finding a rabbit-savvy vet, GI stasis emergency recognition, and the 8-12 year lifespan commitment. The site's first non-dog/cat content.
- [Pet Emergency Kit Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/pet-emergency-kit-checklist.html): Disaster/evacuation preparedness for dogs and cats — documents (vaccination records, microchip, ownership proof), 3-7 day food/water/medication supply, carrier/leash/litter supplies, and an evacuation plan (pet-friendly hotels, out-of-area contact, rescue alert sticker). Universal, not species-specific.

- [Puppy Socialization Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/puppy-socialization-checklist.html): 26 items across people, sounds, surfaces/floors, transport, handling (paws/ears/mouth), other animals, and environments. Enter the puppy's birthdate for a live countdown to the end of the critical 16-week socialization window. Includes an AVSAB-sourced section on why socialization shouldn't wait for full vaccination, paired with safety caveats (avoid dog parks/pet stores; favor controlled settings).

- [Kitten Socialization Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/kitten-socialization-checklist.html): 24 items across people, handling (paws/ears/mouth), surfaces, sounds, carrier training, nail-care tool exposure, and other animals. Framed around a key fact most kitten guides omit: the primary sensitive period (2-7 weeks, Karsh 1983; Karsh & Turner 1988) is usually over before most owners even meet their kitten, since typical adoption age is 8-12 weeks — so the tool's real value is the secondary window (roughly 9-16 weeks) and catch-up socialization. Countdown widget targets the end of that secondary window rather than the (usually already-closed) primary one. Cites Casey & Bradshaw (2008, Applied Animal Behaviour Science) on additional-socialization outcomes for older/rescue kittens. Explicitly notes vaccine timing is not a comparable gating factor here, unlike the puppy checklist, since most items are controlled/indoor. No brand-name pheromone products recommended (generic "synthetic feline pheromone diffuser" only).

- [New Guinea Pig Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/new-guinea-pig-checklist.html): The site's third non-dog/cat checklist. 20 items covering cage size (7.5 sq ft minimum for one, 10.5+ preferred for a pair), never-alone social housing requirement (legally mandated in some countries), vitamin C (can't be synthesized, unlike most mammals), alfalfa-only-under-6-months hay rule, cedar/pine bedding and wire-flooring hazards, and a 5-7 year lifespan commitment.

- [Senior Pet Care Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/senior-pet-care-checklist.html): 20 items for dogs and cats covering vet screening (twice-yearly visits, senior blood panel components by name only, dental and joint assessment as commonly under-diagnosed conditions), home comfort changes (non-slip flooring, ramps, orthopedic beds, lower-entry litter boxes, ramps/steps to elevated cat perches), bidirectional weight monitoring, and behavioral observation (new confusion, disorientation, or house-soiling framed as "log and mention to your vet," not a diagnostic tool). Deliberately frames aging as a normal life stage, not a disease, and excludes euthanasia/end-of-life content, which is covered elsewhere on the site.

- [Moving With Pets Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/moving-with-pets-checklist.html): 24 items organized by countdown (4 weeks before, 2 weeks before, 1 week before, moving day, first week after). Covers microchip address updates (the most commonly forgotten step), the moving-day safe-room/"Do Not Open" sign protocol to prevent escapes, gradual room-by-room introduction at the new home, keeping a cat's existing litter box unchanged to prevent regression (linked to the litter-training-regression post), a 2-3 week indoor-only period for cats before outdoor access, and researching destination pet registration/leash/breed rules.

- [Post-Surgery Recovery Checklist](https://petpawcalc.com/checklists/post-surgery-recovery-checklist.html): 22 items for major/orthopedic procedures (TPLO, other CCL/ACL repairs), explicitly distinct from the existing Spay/Neuter Recovery Timeline's much shorter 10-14 day scale. Covers pre-surgery home prep, the first 48 hours, and 8-12 weeks of strict activity restriction. Centers on the most common recovery mistake — loosening restrictions once a dog "feels better" around weeks 3-6, well before the bone has actually finished healing on recheck imaging. Fixed "your vet's discharge instructions always take priority" warning at page top and in the disclaimer. No dosage/medication content.

## Blog

- [How to Calculate Your Dog's Age in Human Years (It's Not 7x)](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-age-human-years): PetMD's size-based rule with a chart by age and size, the 2020 Cell Systems epigenetic clock (16 × ln(age) + 31, mostly Labradors), senior ages by size (PetMD, VCA) and cognitive decline.

- [How Much Does a Dog Really Cost Per Year?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/annual-cost-of-owning-a-dog): Rover 2026 figures ($145–$505/month for a medium dog, $39,350 median lifetime), the ASPCA category and first-year tables, national average vet prices (Synchrony 2025–26), NAPHIA 2025 insurance premiums ($836 accident-and-illness), and emergency cost ranges.

- [How Much Should I Feed My Dog?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-to-feed-a-dog): Daily calories from resting energy requirement × Merck life-stage multipliers, a 10–90 lb calorie table, adjusting by body condition, treats, free-feeding, and the Labrador POMC mutation.

- [How Much Should a Senior Dog Eat?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-should-senior-dog-eat): When dogs count as senior by size (VCA), the 12–13% fall in energy needs, a 1.4 × RER starting table, AAHA 2023 guidance on protein, calorie density and fibre, and weight and muscle changes that need a vet.

- [Puppy Weight Chart by Breed Size](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/puppy-weight-chart-by-breed-size): When toy to giant puppies stop growing (PetMD), the vet rules for estimating adult weight at 6–8 weeks or 4 months, expected weekly gain by adult size (Merck), why large-breed puppies shouldn't grow fast, and growth-diet guidance.
- [Kitten Weight Chart by Age](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/kitten-weight-chart-by-breed-size): ASPCA weekly kitten weights for weeks 1–8, the ASPCA's about-a-pound-per-month rule, VCA's growth milestones (80% of adult size at 30 weeks, adult size at 40), large-breed weights and maturity ages (APOP), and when slow gain needs a vet.

- [Why Is My Cat Always Hungry?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/why-is-my-cat-always-hungry): Checking the amount against RER × Merck multipliers, how cats' needs change with age (AAHA, VCA), medical causes of increased appetite such as hyperthyroidism and diabetes, and telling hunger from habit.

- [How to Tell If Your Dog Is Overweight](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-dog-is-overweight): The rib, waist and tuck checks, the 9-point body condition scale, ~10% excess weight per point above 5 and 1–2% weekly loss (AAHA 2014), 59% of US dogs overweight (APOP 2022), and the Kealy Labrador lifespan study.

- [The True Cost of Owning a Cat vs Dog](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/true-cost-cat-vs-dog-year-by-year): Cat vs medium dog side by side — Rover 2026 monthly, senior and lifetime costs ($32,527 vs $39,350 median), ASPCA first-year and annual tables, NAPHIA premiums ($435 vs $836) and Synchrony vet prices.

- [How Often Should You Take Your Dog to the Vet?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-often-vet-visits-dog-cost-by-age): Puppy visits every 3–4 weeks to 16–20 weeks, yearly adult checkups and six-monthly senior visits (PetMD), what each visit covers, and Synchrony average prices for the exam, vaccines and senior bloodwork.
- [Flea & Tick Prevention Cost for Dogs and Cats](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/flea-tick-prevention-cost): Yearly cost of Seresto, Frontline Plus, NexGard, Simparica Trio and Revolution Plus at Chewy prices (Nov 2026), CAPC's year-round recommendation, the FDA-approved Bravecto Quantum yearly injection, and clearing an infestation.

- [Puppy Potty Training Regression: Why It Happens (and How to Fix It)](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/puppy-potty-training-regression): When regression happens, ruling out medical causes first, behavioral causes and the house-training reset plan from veterinary behaviorist Kelly Ballantyne, and why punishment backfires.

- [Cat Litter Training Regression: Why a Trained Cat Suddenly Stops](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/kitten-litter-training-regression): Vet check first, feline idiopathic cystitis and urethral obstruction (Cornell), non-medical causes and marking, and the FelineVMA litter box setup (n+1 boxes, 1.5× body length, unscented clumping litter, daily scooping).

- [How to Tell If Your Dog Is Underweight (and How to Help Them Gain Weight Safely)](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-dog-is-underweight): At-home rib, spine and muscle checks, underweight versus naturally lean sighthounds, common medical causes, and gradual weight gain for a healthy dog after a vet check.

- [How to Tell If Your Cat Is Underweight or Too Skinny (and When It's Urgent)](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-cat-is-underweight): The WSAVA 9-point body condition descriptions for scores 1–5, the WSAVA muscle condition score (normal to marked loss over spine, shoulder blades, skull and hips) and why a cat can look bony at a normal weight (sarcopenia vs cachexia), why monthly weighing matters (weight loss about 2.5 years before death from cancer, CKD or hyperthyroidism; about 3 years before a CKD diagnosis), common medical causes with links to cost guides, urgent signs and hepatic lipidosis (Cornell), and how to help a cat regain weight.

- [How Much Does a Vet Visit Cost?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-does-a-vet-visit-cost): National average prices from the 2025–26 Synchrony veterinary cost study (exam $56–$129, vaccines, bloodwork, X-rays, ultrasound, dental), PetMD ranges and checkup schedule, diagnostic workup totals, Preventive Vet emergency costs and NAPHIA premiums.

- [How Long Are Dogs Pregnant? A Week-by-Week Guide](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-long-are-dogs-pregnant/): About 63 days from ovulation, 63 ± 7 days from mating (Cornell); week-by-week table with implantation (~day 18), ultrasound (from ~3 weeks, reliable after day 28), relaxin (after day 22–27), X-ray (day 42–45; count after day 55) per Merck/VCA; feeding unchanged for the first two thirds then up to 1.5×; temperature drop below 99°F; when to call the vet.

- [What to Feed a Pregnant Dog: Diet, Portions, and the Timing That Matters](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/what-to-feed-pregnant-dog/): Maintenance intake for the first two thirds, at least +20–30% in the last third (Merck), up to 1.5× in the last three weeks (VCA), 2–4× maintenance while nursing with free-choice feeding, growth diet from the start of pregnancy, why calcium supplements are discouraged.

- [How to Tell If Your Dog Is Pregnant: Early Signs and Vet Confirmation](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-dog-is-pregnant/): Why at-home signs are unreliable, false pregnancy (4–9 weeks after heat, most intact females show signs, settles in 2–3 weeks — VCA; 87% figure — AKC), and confirmation by ultrasound, relaxin, palpation and X-ray with timings (Merck, VCA).

- [Signs of Dog Labor: What to Expect Hour by Hour](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/signs-of-dog-labor/): Temperature drop, stage 1 (6–12 hours of signs, up to 24–36 hours), stage 2 timings (0–30 minutes per puppy, up to 2 hours between), placentas, lochia for about 3 weeks (Cornell), dystocia criteria and prevalence (Merck), when to call the vet.

- [How to Reduce Vet Costs Without Compromising Your Dog's Care](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-reduce-vet-costs-for-dogs): Prevention that pays for itself (heartworm, vaccines, dental, spay) with prices, checkup schedule, emergency planning with insurance or savings, asking about tests, comparing estimates and the ASPCA's money-saving list.

- [How Often Should Cats Go to the Vet? A Schedule by Age](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-often-vet-visits-cat): AAHA/AAFP feline life stages, kitten visits to 16–20 weeks, yearly adult and six-monthly senior checkups (PetMD, VCA), why indoor cats still need them, average prices and making visits less stressful.

- [How Long Are Cats Pregnant? A Week-by-Week Guide](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-long-are-cats-pregnant/): About 63–65 days on average, range about 60–67 (some to 71) per VCA; trimester table, confirmation timing, feeding (+50% in pregnancy, over 2× by end of nursing), nesting box, signs of impending birth, postpartum complications.

- [How to Tell If Your Cat Is Pregnant: Early Signs and Vet Confirmation](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-cat-is-pregnant/): Induced ovulation and pregnancy while nursing; signs by trimester across a 63–65-day pregnancy (pinking up at days 16–20); vet confirmation by palpation (~2½ weeks), ultrasound heartbeats (3–4 weeks; scans before day 21 can miss it, per Merck) and X-ray (~6 weeks, to count kittens); rare pseudopregnancy; temperature below 100°F before labor (PetMD).

- [What to Feed a Pregnant Cat: Diet, Portions, and Why Cats Need More From the Start](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/what-to-feed-pregnant-cat/): Queens gain weight steadily from conception, unlike dogs (Merck); kitten/growth food with AAFCO gestation/lactation or all-life-stages claims (VCA); last-third intake +25% average and energy up to 40% above maintenance; 2–3× intake while nursing; free-choice feeding for 3–4 weeks except with one or two kittens (mastitis risk); foods and supplements to avoid.

- [Signs of Cat Labor: What to Expect Before, During, and After](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/signs-of-cat-labor/): Pre-labor signs (temperature below 100°F, stops eating, milk 24–48 hours before), stage timings, 10–60 minutes between kittens, normal interrupted labor of 24–36 hours, VCA's call-the-vet list, nest temperatures and postpartum complications.

- [How Much Should a Cat Weigh?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-should-a-cat-weigh): Breed reference weights from APOP, the 8–12 lb domestic shorthair range (PetMD), body condition score 5 as ideal, when large breeds finish growing, and safe weight loss.

- [How Much Does a Cat Vet Visit Cost?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-does-a-cat-vet-visit-cost): Synchrony 2025–26 average cat prices (exam $57–$130, FVRCP, rabies, dental $395), a healthy cat's yearly vet cost, and cat-specific big bills — urinary blockage, tooth resorption, hyperthyroidism, kidney disease, outdoor injuries.

- [How to Reduce Vet Costs Without Compromising Your Cat's Care](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-reduce-vet-costs-for-cats): Making checkups happen for a fearful cat, senior bloodwork, the urinary emergency not to wait on, dental care, prevention prices, keeping cats lean, and insurance at about $435 a year (NAPHIA).

- [How Much Should a Senior Cat Eat?](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-much-should-senior-cat-eat): Why cats' energy needs rise again from about 10–11 years, a 1.2 × RER starting table, why healthy seniors need more protein not less (AAHA 2023), meal frequency, water and the weight changes that need a vet.

- [Dog Quality of Life: How to Assess Your Dog's Well-Being](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-quality-of-life-assessment): Using Villalobos's HHHHHMM scale (seven areas, 0–10, above 35 of 70 acceptable), what to look for in each area, tracking the trend, treatable causes of a low score, and chronic pain signs (AAHA 2022).

- [Cat Quality of Life: How to Read the Signs Cats Hide, and How to Score Them](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/cat-quality-of-life-assessment/): Behavioral signs of pain in cats (FVMA; arthritis signs in up to 92% of cats), the Feline Grimace Scale (five facial features scored 0–2, ≥4/10 indicates pain), a cat-specific HHHHHMM table, treatable causes of low scores (arthritis, dental pain, kidney dehydration, appetite drugs Mirataz and Elura, hormone disorders, home changes), hepatic lipidosis risk, logging and end-of-life decisions.

- [How to Tell If Your Cat Is Overweight](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/how-to-tell-if-cat-is-overweight): Rib, waist and belly checks, the primordial pouch, the WSAVA 9-point scale with 5 as ideal, 61% of US cats overweight (APOP 2022), safe loss of 0.5–2% a week (AAHA) and the hepatic lipidosis risk of crash diets.

- [Puppy and Kitten Vaccination Schedule: The Complete Guide](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/puppy-kitten-vaccination-schedule): AAHA 2022 canine and AAHA/AAFP 2020 feline schedules — core series, boosters, 3-year adult intervals, leptospirosis, Bordetella, influenza, Lyme, FeLV and rabies — with Synchrony average vaccine prices.

- [Spay or Neuter Your Pet: Cost, Timing, and What to Expect](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/spay-neuter-cost-and-timing): Synchrony average prices (dog spay $455, cat spay $353), AAHA 2019 size-based timing for dogs, the fix-by-five-months standard for cats, and ASPCA recovery instructions.

- [Dog and Cat Dental Cleaning Cost: What to Expect](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/dog-cat-dental-cleaning-cost): Average cleaning prices ($379 dog, $395 cat) plus X-rays and extractions, why the AVDC rejects anesthesia-free scaling, periodontal disease by age 2 (Merck), and home care that works.

- [Pet Euthanasia: What It Costs and What to Expect](https://petpawcalc.com/blog/pet-euthanasia-cost-and-what-to-expect): Clinic ($120–$130 average for dogs) and at-home (about $450) costs from PetMD, Lap of Love surcharges, cremation and burial prices, what happens during the appointment, and questions to ask.

## About

PetPawCalc is focused on a single niche: calculators and practical guides for US pet owners. All tools are free, require no account, and are designed to give immediately usable outputs. Content follows veterinary guidelines and includes disclaimers where appropriate. The site does not provide medical diagnoses or medication dosing.

Contact: canghun13@naver.com
